_comment: Pipeline honeypot → deteção: para cada path-isco do Worker (dynamic/worker/src/index.js, DECOYS), a regra Sigma que apanharia a mesma atividade num SIEM. Os paths e as técnicas TÊM de coincidir com content/honeypot-attack.json (há um teste no worker que verifica a sincronização). O YAML vive como array de linhas (join com \n) para ser legível em JSON; campos de field mapping seguem as convenções webserver do SigmaHQ (c-uri, cs-method, sc-status). Texto PT em português europeu.

summary.pt: O path mais tentado da Internet: botnets à procura de logins WordPress para força bruta de credenciais. Em infraestrutura que não serve WordPress, qualquer pedido a este path é hostil por definição — a regra dispara ao primeiro toque, sem thresholds.
summary.en: The most-tried path on the Internet: botnets hunting WordPress logins to brute-force credentials. On infrastructure that does not serve WordPress, any request for this path is hostile by definition — the rule fires on first touch, no thresholds.

sigma: title: WordPress Login Probe On Non-WordPress Infrastructure
Detects requests to /wp-login.php on infrastructure that does not run
WordPress. Automated botnets probe this path to brute-force credentials
(observed continuously by the honeypot at danielmala.co/honeypot). On a
non-WordPress estate this is high-fidelity: there is no legitimate reason
- Estates that actually run WordPress — there, scope to failed logins
(cs-method POST + sc-status 200 burst) or add per-source thresholds

summary.pt: Ficheiros dotenv guardam segredos (chaves de API, credenciais de BD) e ficam expostos por deploys descuidados. Os scanners pedem-nos a todos os hosts que encontram. Um pedido a /.env nunca é tráfego legítimo — é reconhecimento à procura de segredos.
summary.en: Dotenv files hold secrets (API keys, DB credentials) and get exposed by careless deploys. Scanners request them from every host they find. A request for /.env is never legitimate traffic — it is reconnaissance hunting for secrets.

sigma: title: Environment File Requested Over HTTP (.env)
Detects HTTP requests for .env files. Dotenv files hold credentials and
API keys; scanners probe every discovered host for them after years of
accidental exposures. There is no legitimate reason for a client to
request /.env (observed daily by the honeypot at danielmala.co/honeypot).
- Unlikely — internal tooling that legitimately fetches dotenv files over
HTTP would itself be a finding

summary.pt: Um /.git/ acessível permite reconstruir o código-fonte inteiro do site (e os segredos committados por engano). Os scanners começam pelo /.git/config porque confirma a exposição com um único pedido. Deteção de primeiro toque, como o /.env.
summary.en: An accessible /.git/ lets an attacker reconstruct the site's entire source (and any secrets committed by mistake). Scanners start with /.git/config because it confirms the exposure with a single request. First-touch detection, like /.env.

sigma: Detects HTTP requests for /.git/config. A web-accessible .git directory
allows full source (and committed-secret) reconstruction with public
tooling; scanners request the config file first because it confirms the
exposure in one hit (observed by the honeypot at danielmala.co/honeypot).
- None expected — legitimate git traffic uses the smart HTTP endpoints

summary.pt: Enumeração clássica de superfície: os scanners percorrem listas de paths de administração conhecidos à procura de consolas esquecidas. Num host sem painel /admin é sinal inequívoco de scanning ativo — mas em estates com aplicações reais o path pode existir, daí o nível mais baixo e a nota de tuning.
summary.en: Classic surface enumeration: scanners walk lists of well-known admin paths hunting for forgotten consoles. On a host with no /admin panel it is an unambiguous sign of active scanning — but real estates may serve the path legitimately, hence the lower level and the tuning note.

sigma: Detects requests to /admin on hosts that do not serve an admin panel.
Part of automated active-scanning wordlists that enumerate well-known
administrative paths (observed by the honeypot at
danielmala.co/honeypot). Scope the rule to hosts where the path does
not exist, or correlate bursts across many 404s from one source.
- Applications that really serve /admin — exclude those hosts or drop
the rule where the panel is expected

summary.pt: O phpMyAdmin exposto é um alvo perene de exploits públicos e credenciais por omissão — dá acesso direto à base de dados. Os scanners tentam o path para encontrar instalações esquecidas e explorá-las como ponto de entrada. Sem phpMyAdmin no estate, primeiro toque = deteção.
summary.en: Exposed phpMyAdmin is a perennial target of public exploits and default credentials — it hands over direct database access. Scanners try the path to find forgotten installs and exploit them as an entry point. With no phpMyAdmin in the estate, first touch = detection.

sigma: title: phpMyAdmin Probe On Estate Without phpMyAdmin
Detects requests to /phpmyadmin/ paths. Exposed phpMyAdmin installs are
a long-standing initial-access vector (public exploits, default
credentials, direct DB access); automated scanners probe the path on
every host (observed by the honeypot at danielmala.co/honeypot). On an
estate that does not run phpMyAdmin this is high-fidelity.
- Estates that legitimately run phpMyAdmin — there, scope to
authentication failures and unusual source networks instead
